title: Safely managed sanitation, Least developed countries (LDCs), by location
headline: In LDCs, safely managed sanitation for all by 2030 needs coverage to rise 12.2 points a year
subtitle: Proportion of population using an improved sanitation facility that is not shared with other households, from which excreta are safely disposed of in situ or removed and treated off-site
years: So far it has risen 0.5 points a year, from 14.3% in 2000 to 27.0% in 2024.
data_line: Data: WHO/UNICEF JMP via UN SDG Global Database, series SH_SAN_SAFE, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: In LDCs, safely managed sanitation for all by 2030 needs coverage to rise 12.2 points a year. So far it has risen 0.5 points a year, from 14.3% in 2000 to 27.0% in 2024. People using safely managed sanitation, Least developed countries (LDCs): 14.3% in 2000, 27.0% in 2024. At that pace about 30.2% in 2030; reaching 100% needs 12.2 points a year.
method: Method: linear pace, 2000 to 2024; target year 2030.
question: Where has safely managed sanitation moved at anything like 12.2 points a year, and what made it possible?
